q: 1. To which category do the chromite bricks belong?
explain: Chromite bricks are neutral refractory bricks; they are resistant to both acidic and basic slags and are used in furnaces for various metals.

q: 2. Minimum thickness of wall where single Flemish bond can be used is ...............
options: one and a half brick thick
explain: Single Flemish bond uses Flemish bond for the face and English bond for the backing. It requires at least a 1.5-brick thick wall to accommodate this structural transition.

q: 3. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads is ...............
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brickwork because it has no continuous vertical joints between courses, making it ideal for load-bearing walls.

q: 4. As compared to English bond, double Flemish bond is ...............
explain: English bond is the strongest so D is Correct

q: 5. The portion of a brick cut to form angles other than right angles in plan, is known as ...............
explain: Squint bricks are specially cut or molded bricks used to form oblique (non-90 degree) corners in wall construction.

q: 6. Refractory bricks resist ...............
explain: They are specifically designed for lining furnaces, kilns, and boilers to withstand extreme heat (often over ) without softening or melting.

q: 7. The main ingredient of a good quality brick earth, is ............
explain: Alumina is the primary constituent of brick earth , preventing the brick from cracking, shrinking, and warping.

q: 8. Clay and silt content in a good brick earth must be at least ............
explain: A good brick earth should contain about 50% silica and a combined total of clay and silt around 50% to ensure proper plasticity and strength.

q: 9. Pug mill is the device used for ............
options: excavating the soil for preparation of bricks
tempering the earth needed for manufacture of bricks
explain: Pug mills are used for tempering (kneading) the brick earth to achieve a plastic mass of uniform across the whole mixture.

q: 10. When a brick is cut into two halves longitudinally, one part is called ............
explain: A queen closer is a brick piece cut in half along its length, used to close the bond at the end of a course.

q: 11. A brick which is given a wedge like shape to be used in the construction of arches is called
explain: Voussoirs are wedge-shaped units (bricks or stones) used in the construction of an arch or a vault.

q: 12. The red colour obtained by the bricks is due to the presence of ............
explain: Iron oxide in brick earth (usually 5-6%) imparts the characteristic red color to the bricks upon burning.

q: 13. Formation of whitish deposit on the bricks due to the presence of excess salts is called ......
explain: Efflorescence is a crystalline deposit of salts that forms on the surface of brickwork when water evaporates.

q: 14. Hollow bricks are generally used with the purpose of ............
explain: The air trapped inside hollow bricks acts as an excellent thermal insulator, keeping the building cool in summer and warm in winter.

q: 15. Tiles are used for ............
explain: Tiles are versatile building units used for aesthetic floorings, weather protection on roofs, and lining for drains/sewers.

q: 16. The frog of the brick is normally made on its .............
explain: The 'frog' is an indentation made on the top face of a brick to form a key for the mortar and to reduce the weight of the brick.

q: 17. The operation of removal of impurities of clay adhering to iron ore is known as ............
explain: Dressing is the mechanical process of cleaning the ore to remove impurities like clay, sand, and stones before the chemical smelting process begins.

q: 18. The weight of a good quality brick when immersed in water for a period of 16 hours should not exceed the weight of dry brick ............
explain: A standard first-class brick should not absorb more than 20% of its dry weight in water, ensuring it is dense and durable.

q: 19. The weight of 1 m³ of brick earth, is about ............
explain: Brick earth (uncompacted soil for brick making) generally has a density of approximately 1800 kg/m³.

q: 20. The main function of alumina in brick earth is ............
explain: Alumina (clay) is the ingredient that makes the soil plastic, allowing the brick earth to be molded into shape.

q: 21. The percentage of alumina in a good brick earth lies between ............
explain: A desirable brick earth contains 20-30% Alumina. Too little reduces plasticity; too much causes cracking during drying.

q: 22. Excess of alumina in brick earth makes the brick ............
options: to crack and warp on drying
explain: While alumina provides plasticity, an excess amount results in high shrinkage during the drying and burning stages, leading to warping and cracks.

q: 23. Percentage of silica in good brick earth lies between ............
explain: Silica (sand) forms the bulk of a brick (50-60%) and prevents the brick from shrinking, cracking, or warping.

q: 24. Excess of silica in brick earth results in ............
explain: Too much silica makes the brick brittle and reduces the cohesion between particles, leading to a weak brick that can easily break.

q: 25. In a brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as ............
explain: Flemish bond involves placing one header and one stretcher alternately in every course. If both faces show this, it's a Double Flemish bond.

q: 26. For what purpose are fire bricks used ............
options: to protect the building against lightning
explain: Fire bricks (refractory bricks) are designed to withstand high temperatures and act as thermal insulators to prevent heat loss/flow in furnaces and kilns.

q: 27. The portion of the brick without a triangular corner equal to half the width and half the length is called
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting off a triangular corner from one end, such that the cut width is half the original width and the cut length is half the original length.

q: 28. The FROG is provided in the bricks for ............
explain: The primary technical purpose of a frog is to create a mechanical 'key' that interlocks the brick with the mortar layer.

q: 29. Bricks produced by washing the inside surface of the brick mould with water are known as ...
explain: Slop moulding involves wetting the mold with water to prevent the clay from sticking, resulting in a smoother finish than sand moulding.

q: 30. The rocks in which argil (or clay) pre-dominates, are called ............
explain: Argillaceous rocks (like slate or shale) are sedimentary rocks where clay is the main component.

q: 31. The size of modular bricks, is ............
explain: The standard or modular size of a brick is 19 cm x 9 cm x 9 cm; when mortar joints are included, it becomes 20 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm.

q: 32. The term frog means ............
options: an apparatus to lift the stone
a depression on a face of brick
vertical joint in a brick work
explain: A frog is an indentation made on the top face of a brick to form a key for the mortar and sometimes to hold the manufacturer's name.

q: 33. Which of the following ingredients of the brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica (sand) prevents cracking, shrinking, and warping of raw bricks, thus helping them retain their shape during drying and burning.

q: 34. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is known as ............
explain: Kneading is the mechanical process of grinding and mixing clay with water to make it plastic and ready for moulding.

q: 35. Bricks manufactured by clearing the inside surface of the brick mould with sand are known as ............
explain: In sand moulding, sand is sprinkled on the inner sides of the mould to prevent the wet clay from sticking to it.

q: 36. Machine moulding of bricks can be done by ............
explain: Industrial brick manufacturing uses both plastic clay (wire-cut) machines and dry-press machines depending on the moisture content of the clay.

q: 37. How many bricks can be moulded per day by a moulder and a helper?
explain: A skilled moulder with a helper can typically produce around 1000 bricks in a standard working day by hand moulding.
